argument:
Path changed: the carry arm of @advsp, i.e. the run whose byte advance carries out of sp's low byte. sp advances 8*rc_n = 32 bytes on a full run, so this is roughly 1 run in 8 (about 2-3 times per 80-char row, out of ~20 runs). The other 7 in 8 fall straight through `bcc :++` and are untouched.

Current carry arm: lda sp+1 (3) + inca (2) + ringup's cmp #>RINGEND (2) + bcc taken (3) + sta sp+1 (3) = 13 cycles, 11 bytes. ringup's `sbc #>RINGBYTES` is never executed (see assumption), so the cmp/bcc pair is pure overhead and the value never needs to pass through A at all. Replacing the whole arm with `inc sp+1` costs 5 cycles and 2 bytes: 8 cycles and 9 bytes saved.

Why the wrap can never be needed here. @advsp has exactly two entries. (a) The copy path: @run computes tmp = 8*rc_n, then `ldy rc_wrap / beq :+` skips the check when rc_wrap = 0, else `adc sp / lda sp+1 / adc #(256 - >RINGEND) / bcc :+ / jmp @slow`. That adc sequence computes exactly sp+1 + carry-out-of-(sp+tmp) and leaves C set iff that result >= >RINGEND; if C is set the run goes to @slow (which does its own ringup through spnext), so reaching jmpx @jt-2 means the new sp+1 is strictly below >RINGEND -- which is the same quantity @advsp recomputes. (b) The solid path at @solid does the identical test and diverts to @fslow with `bcs @fslow`. When rc_wrap = 0, @drawrow set it from `cmp #(>RINGEND - 3)`, so sp+1 <= >RINGEND - 4 at row start, and a row is at most ROWBYTES = 640 bytes = at most 3 page crossings, so sp+1 <= >RINGEND - 1 for the whole row.

Correctness. Flags: the old arm left A = sp+1 and N/Z from ringup's sbc or from inca; the new one leaves A = sp (low sum) and N/Z from inc sp+1. Both are dead -- @runend's first instruction is `lda cnt`, immediately followed by `sec`. C is unchanged by `inc zp` and was already irrelevant (@runend does `sec`). X and Y are untouched by both versions.

Anonymous labels (rule 3): ringup contributes one `:`, so deleting it would renumber `bcc :++`. The proposal therefore keeps a bare `:` placeholder in its place -- exactly the device already used at @fslow ("KEPT, unreferenced, so the anonymous-label count through drawrect is unchanged") and in the blt16i/bge16i macros. `bcc :++` is left byte-for-byte unchanged and still lands on the second label, which is at the same address as the first. Verified with ca65: `bcc :++ / inc $80 / : / :` assembles to 90 02 E6 80, i.e. the branch skips the inc, with only the usual "No reference to unnamed label" warning on the placeholder.

Inlining removes both overheads and, for gx0/gy, the staging entirely. Per call: gx0 was lda wx 3 + sta t16 3 + lda wx+1 3 + sta t16+1 3 + jsr 6 + body 24 + rts 6 + sta gx0 3 = 51 cycles; inlined it is lda wx+1 3 + asl 2 + asl 2 + sta t16+1 3 + lda wx 3 + rol 2 + rol 2 + rol 2 + and #3 2 + ora t16+1 3 + sta gx0 3 = 27, saving 24. gy is identical, saving 24. gx1 was 18 (setup) + 6 + 24 + 6 + 3 = 57; inlined the sta t16+1 is replaced by asl / asl / sta t16+1 acting on the adc #0 result in A, giving 39, saving 18; gy1 likewise 18. Total 84 cycles per frame, 216 -> 132. Correctness: the arithmetic is byte-for-byte shr6's. In the gx0/gy form, asl / asl on the high byte leave C = bit 6 of the high byte, which is 0 because t16 < 16384 means hi < 64; lda wx does not touch C, so the three rols see the same C_in (0) that shr6's did, and and #3 keeps only the two bits of wx shifted down from bits 7 and 6. In the gx1/gy1 form the adc #0 that completes the 16-bit add leaves a carry, but the immediately following asl overwrites C before any rol reads it, exactly as shr6's first asl did after lda t16+1; the low byte is preserved in t16 across the two asls (which only touch A) and reloaded with lda t16. argument:
The left-clip arm stores a known-zero rel into w16/w16+1 and then falls into @right, which immediately loads both bytes back and runs the generic range test on them - a value written and re-read one instruction later, with every branch of the test statically decided. With w16 = 0: 'bne @none' is never taken, 'cmp #ROWCHARS / bcs @none' is never taken, 'adc rc_w' with C=0 yields rc_w, and 'lda #ROWCHARS / sbc w16' with C=1 yields ROWCHARS. So the whole thing collapses to min(rc_w, ROWCHARS), which is what the proposal writes, and the stz pair can go because drawrect rebuilds w16 from rc_x before its first read of it.
Cycles on the left-clipped path: old stz 3 + stz 3 + lda w16+1 3 + bne nt 2 + lda w16 3 + cmp 2 + bcs nt 2 + adc rc_w 3 = 21 before the clamp test; new lda rc_w 3. That is 18 saved when rc_w already fits, and 21 when it is clamped (the old arm also pays lda #ROWCHARS 2 + sbc w16 3 where the new one pays lda #ROWCHARS 2). The unclipped path through @right is byte-identical and unchanged.
Frequency: this arm is taken only when a rect starts left of the window, i.e. the 'bpl @right' above the window falls through. That is a minority of drawrect_clip calls - a sprite-erase rect or dirty cell straddling the window's left edge, typically a small handful a frame - so this is worth 18 cycles a time on a cold-ish arm, not 18 times the call count. Costs 7 bytes.
ANONYMOUS LABEL WARNING: this adds one ':' line. It sits before @right, so the existing 'bcc :+' inside @right still finds its own ':' (which is after it) and the new 'bcc :+' finds the new one. The forward references above the window ('bpl :+' at 2579, 'bcc :+' at 2595) resolve to ':' lines at 2588 and 2600, both ahead of the insertion point, and there is no ':-' in this routine, so nothing counts across the new label.

assumption: px, py, exitx, exity are map pixel coordinates whose difference fits in 16-bit two's complement (they are 16-bit zero-page level coordinates well under $4000, so |px-exitx| < 32768 always). t16 stays free scratch -- the code being replaced already uses it. IMPORTANT: this removes four macro invocations (2x blt16, 2x bge16) that each expand to one ca65 anonymous label, so the anonymous-label count through logic.s drops by 4 at this point. Checked: the nearest anonymous references either side are 'bne :+' at the @bfly tail (which resolves before this block) and 'bpl :-' at line 3096 (far below, with many ':' labels in between), and there is no ':--' or ':++' anywhere in logic.s that could count across the block.
original:
blt16 px, exitx, @noexit
        lda exitx
        clc
        adc #16
        sta t16
        lda exitx+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 px, t16, @noexit
        blt16 py, exity, @noexit
        lda exity
        clc
        adc #24
        sta t16
        lda exity+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 py, t16, @noexit
        lda #1
        sta exiting
proposal:
lda px                      ; inside the exit box is 0 <= px-exitx < 16 and
        sec                         ; 0 <= py-exity < 24: one 16-bit subtract each,
        sbc exitx                   ; high byte zero (so the difference is 0..255)
        sta t16                     ; and low byte under the width
        lda px+1
        sbc exitx+1
        bne @noexit
        lda t16
        cmp #16
        bcs @noexit
        lda py
        sec
        sbc exity
        sta t16
        lda py+1
        sbc exity+1
        bne @noexit
        lda t16
        cmp #24
        bcs @noexit
        lda #1
        sta exiting
argument:
The routine builds the exit box's far corner twice per frame with a 16-bit add into t16 (exitx+16, exity+24), then runs a signed 16-bit compare against each edge -- two signed compares and a 16-bit add per axis, when the whole test is one subtraction. 'exitx <= px < exitx+16' is exactly '0 <= px-exitx < 16', and the 16-bit two's complement difference of two map coordinates represents the true difference exactly, so the high byte of px-exitx is zero if and only if the difference is in 0..255; 'cmp #16 / bcs' then narrows that to 0..15. px < exitx gives a high byte of $FF (or lower) and px >= exitx+256 gives $01 or more -- both non-zero, both rejected by the same bne, so the single test covers what blt16 and bge16 covered together. cmp/bcs here is a genuinely unsigned test on a value already known to be 0..255, not a signed comparison in disguise.

Cycles, per axis: blt16 falling through is 17 (lda/cmp/lda/sbc/bvc taken/bmi not taken), the add is 18, and bge16 taken is 18 -- 53 to reject on the x axis once px is at or past exitx. The replacement is lda 3 + sec 2 + sbc 3 + sta 3 + lda 3 + sbc 3 + bne 2 + lda 3 + cmp 2 + bcs 3 = 27. That is the 26 quoted, on the path where the player is at or right of the exit's x (the path that currently pays for the whole 16-bit add); when both axes are in range the two halves together go from 105 to 53, saving 52. The one path that loses is px < exitx, where blt16 branches out after 18 cycles against 20 -- 2 cycles, once per frame, against 26 to 52 on every other frame. Bytes: 41 per axis (14 + 13 + 14) become 19, so 44 bytes total.

t16+1 is no longer written; nothing reads it (the next instruction on every path is @noexit's rts). A is dead at @noexit and the flags are not consumed after the rts.

assumption: Y is free inside @addr: no caller of @addr (@emit, the P2 block, @setq) holds a live Y across the jsr -- @nfull returns in A, @advance re-does its own tay, and @dur/@lines never touch Y. w16b is a scratch used nowhere else in build_sections (its only reads and writes in this routine are the ones being deleted).
original:
@addr:  lda w16
        sta w16b
        lda w16+1
        sta w16b+1
        cmp #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        lda w16b
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       lda w16b
        sec
        sbc #<RINGCHARS
        sta w16b
        lda w16b+1
        sbc #>RINGCHARS
        sta w16b+1
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        lda w16b+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
proposal:
@addr:  lda w16                     ; low byte in A, high in Y: w16b was only a copy
        ldy w16+1
        cpy #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       clc                         ; the fold is w16 - RINGCHARS + CRTCBASE, so one
        adc #<(CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS)  ; add of the folded constant does both
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        tya
        adc #>(CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS)
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
:       clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        tya
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
argument: @addr does the same 16-bit value two ways: it first copies w16 into w16b (4 zero-page accesses), then reads w16b back to test it, then on the straddle path subtracts RINGCHARS from w16b and writes it back, then reads it a third time to add CRTCBASE. The subtraction and the addition are both 16-bit adds of assembly-time constants, so they fold into one: CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS = $6A0-$8C0 = $FDE0, and ca65 gives #<(CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS)=$E0, #>(CRTCBASE-RINGCHARS)=$FD (verified by assembling). Holding the low byte in A and the high byte in Y removes w16b entirely. Test structure is identical: cpy against the high constant then cmp against the low constant is the same unsigned 16-bit compare the original did with cmp/cmp, and cpy does not disturb A so the low byte survives the high-byte test. I checked all 65536 values of w16: the folded-constant form gives byte-identical SECTAB pairs to the original. Anonymous labels: the original has exactly two ':' lines inside @addr and so does the proposal, so the count through the rest of engine.s is unchanged; 'bcc :++' still lands on the second (no-fold) label and 'bne :+' on the first (fold) label. Cycles: the no-fold path (the common one -- a row only straddles the ring end when w16 >= RINGCHARS-79) goes 39 -> 29, saving 10; the fold path goes 59 -> 31, saving 28. Bytes 49 -> 40 (measured with ca65/cl65). @addr is called 3-4 times per build_sections call (once per @emit, once for P2 when wfine>0, once at @setq), once per frame.

assumption: For the bvy half only, the dropped 'sta t16+1' relies on logic.s line 1761 -- the 'sta t16+1' that follows the second ldx #6 / cmp #$80 / ror / ror t16 / dex / bne :- loop, four lines past the end of this window -- being present exactly as it is for the bvx half, which is visible in the window. I read logic.s:1757-1762 to confirm it is character-for-character the same tail. If that is not wanted, keep the plain 'sub16 t16, bvy' macro for the second half and the window still saves 6+9 = 15 cycles.
original:
lda bvx
        asl
        sta t16
        lda bvx+1
        rol
        sta t16+1
        add16 t16, bvx
        neg16 t16                   ; leaves A = t16+1
        ldx #6
:       cmp #$80
        ror
        ror t16
        dex
        bne :-
        sta t16+1
        add16 bvx, t16
        asl16 rx
        add16 bvx, rx
        lda bvx
        cmp #$80                    ; C = bit 7 of bvx = carry out of (bvx + 128)
        lda bvx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of bvx + 128
        sx16 t16
        add16 bx, t16
        lda bvy
        asl
        sta t16
        lda bvy+1
        rol
        sta t16+1
        add16 t16, bvy
        neg16 t16                   ; leaves A = t16+1
        ldx #6
proposal:
sec                         ; t16 = -bvx: negate first, then double in place
        lda #0
        sbc bvx
        sta t16
        lda #0
        sbc bvx+1
        sta t16+1
        asl16 t16                   ; t16 = -2*bvx
        sec
        lda t16
        sbc bvx
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        sbc bvx+1                   ; A = high byte of -3*bvx (t16+1 store is dead)
        ldx #6
:       cmp #$80
        ror
        ror t16
        dex
        bne :-
        sta t16+1
        add16 bvx, t16
        asl16 rx
        add16 bvx, rx
        lda bvx
        cmp #$80                    ; C = bit 7 of bvx = carry out of (bvx + 128)
        lda bvx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of bvx + 128
        sx16 t16
        add16 bx, t16
        sec                         ; t16 = -bvy, same shape as the bvx block above
        lda #0
        sbc bvy
        sta t16
        lda #0
        sbc bvy+1
        sta t16+1
        asl16 t16                   ; t16 = -2*bvy
        sec
        lda t16
        sbc bvy
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        sbc bvy+1                   ; A = high byte of -3*bvy (t16+1 store is dead)
        ldx #6
argument: Both halves of the boomerang friction step compute t16 = -(3*v) the same way: copy-and-double (lda v / asl / sta t16 / lda v+1 / rol / sta t16+1 = 16 cy, 10 by), add16 t16,v (20 cy, 13 by), neg16 t16 (18 cy, 13 by) = 54 cy, 36 by. The copy and the negate are the same copy done twice. Negating first makes the doubling an in-place shift: explicit neg of v into t16 (sec/lda #0/sbc v/sta t16/lda #0/sbc v+1/sta t16+1 = 2+2+3+3+2+3+3 = 18 cy, 13 by; v is zero page, bvx=$0E-ish/.zeropage, t16=$D1), asl16 t16 = asl t16 (5) + rol t16+1 (5) = 10 cy, 4 by, giving -2v, then the sub16 body sec/lda t16/sbc v/sta t16/lda t16+1/sbc v+1 = 2+3+3+3+3+3 = 17 cy, 11 by, giving -3v with A = high byte. Total 45 cy, 28 by: 9 cy and 8 by saved per half, 18 cy and 16 by for the two. Arithmetic: ((0-v)*2)-v = -3v mod 2^16, identical to -((2v)+v) mod 2^16 that the original computes; there is no intermediate that is used, so no overflow difference. The trailing 'sta t16+1' of the sub16 expansion is omitted deliberately: the only reader of t16+1 before it is rewritten is 'sta t16+1' immediately after the ldx #6 / cmp #$80 / ror / ror t16 / dex / bne :- loop (that loop reads only A and t16), and add16 bvx,t16 / add16 bvy,t16 then read the value the loop stored. neg16 in the original had the same dead store; this just stops paying for it. Flags: the old sequence ended with sta (flags from sbc t16+1); the new one ends with sbc v+1 (flags from the same kind of subtraction) and the next instruction is ldx #6, which reloads N/Z, followed by cmp #$80 which sets C, so nothing downstream reads them. Carry: asl16 leaves C from bit 7 of t16+1, and the following sec restores it before the subtract chain. Registers: A is the live value across the block as before; X is written by the ldx #6 that follows, exactly as before; Y is untouched by both forms. Anonymous labels: the quoted span contains exactly one ':' line (the shift loop) in both original and proposal, and the macros used (add16, sub16-body written out, asl16, neg16) define none; sx16 defines one and is unchanged in both. So no ':+' / ':-' count changes. Path and frequency: this is the boomerang-physics arm of player_update, reached once per frame whenever bactive != 0 and bcnt < 8. bcnt is wrapped to 0 at 8 by @bfly, so while the boomerang is in flight this arm runs on every frame; it is skipped only when the boomerang is inactive or in its 8..13 landing count. Both halves are on that one path, so the 18 cycles are saved together, once per frame of boomerang flight.

assumption: w16b is scratch for @addr alone: build_sections' only reads and writes of it are the ones inside @addr (engine.s:2362-2382), and every caller of @addr reloads A on the next instruction and never reads w16b.
original:
@addr:  lda w16
        sta w16b
        lda w16+1
        sta w16b+1
        cmp #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        lda w16b
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       lda w16b
        sec
        sbc #<RINGCHARS
        sta w16b
        lda w16b+1
        sbc #>RINGCHARS
        sta w16b+1
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        lda w16b+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
proposal:
@addr:  lda w16+1                   ; no w16b copy: the wrap and the CRTCBASE bias fold
        cmp #>(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1) ; into one add or one subtract, straight into SECTAB
        bcc :++
        bne :+
        lda w16
        cmp #<(RINGCHARS-ROWCHARS+1)
        bcc :++
:       lda w16                     ; straddles: w16 - RINGCHARS + CRTCBASE
        sec
        sbc #<(RINGCHARS-CRTCBASE)
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        lda w16+1
        sbc #>(RINGCHARS-CRTCBASE)
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
:       lda w16                     ; whole row: w16 + CRTCBASE
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        lda w16+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        rts
argument: @addr copies w16 into w16b purely so it can be modified, subtracts RINGCHARS on the straddle path, then adds CRTCBASE on both paths. The subtract and the add are both constants applied to the same 16-bit value, so they fold: w16 - RINGCHARS + CRTCBASE == w16 - (RINGCHARS - CRTCBASE). With RINGCHARS = ROWCHARS*RINGROWS = 80*28 = 2240 and CRTCBASE = RINGBASE/8 = $3500/8 = 1696, the folded constant is 544 = $0220 -- positive, so #<(RINGCHARS-CRTCBASE) = $20 and #>(RINGCHARS-CRTCBASE) = $02, and ca65 needs no negative-constant games. Folding lets the whole w16b temporary go: the range test reads w16 directly and each arm writes SECTAB+1,x / SECTAB,x once. The arithmetic is bit-identical mod 65536; the sbc chain still starts from `sec` and the adc chain from `clc`. Cycles, no-wrap arm (old): lda w16 3, sta w16b 3, lda w16+1 3, sta w16b+1 3, cmp 2, bcc taken 3 = 17, then lda w16b 3, clc 2, adc 2, sta abs,x 5, lda w16b+1 3, adc 2, sta abs,x 5 = 22; 39 before the rts. New: lda w16+1 3, cmp 2, bcc taken 3 = 8, plus the same 22 = 30. Saving 9. Straddle arm (old): 19 to reach the wrap block, 18 for the sbc-into-w16b block, 22 for the add block = 59; new 10 + 22 = 32, saving 27. Bytes 49 -> 46. Anonymous labels are preserved exactly -- two ':' lines before, two after, in the same order -- so `bcc :++` still lands on the second label (now the whole-row arm) and `bne :+` on the first (the straddle arm), and no branch anywhere else changes its count. X is untouched and still indexes the live SECTAB entry; Y is untouched. Path: @addr is called once from @emit (itself run once or twice a frame) and once each from @past and @setq, so three or four times per build_sections, which runs once per frame. At most one of those calls takes the straddle arm, so the per-frame figure is about 27 cycles, rising to roughly 54 on frames where a row straddles the ring end.

assumption: Y is dead after this block (next use is the 'ldy #5' at the record-rect code, engine.s:1276) and X is dead after it (next use is 'ldx curbuf', engine.s:1268); w16/w16+1 are dead here, both being rewritten at @nc (engine.s:1220-1225) before any read. jsr sext touches neither X nor Y (engine.s:3635).
original:
sbc tmp3
        sta w16+1
        txa
        sec
        sbc wy
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        sbc wy+1
        sta sp_lb0+1
        lda w16
        asl                         ; C = old bit 7, exactly what 'asl w16' left
        rol sp_lb0+1
proposal:
sbc tmp3
        tay
        txa
        sec
        sbc wy
        tax
        tya
        sbc wy+1
        sta sp_lb0+1
        txa
        asl                         ; C = old bit 7, exactly what 'asl w16' left
        rol sp_lb0+1
argument: This is the vertical half of drawsprite's clip setup, executed once per drawsprite call, on every path that gets past the horizontal reject. It does exactly the job the horizontal half does twenty lines earlier (spx - refx - wx), and the horizontal half already does it the cheap way: it holds the intermediate high byte in Y via tay/tya (2+2 cycles) instead of parking it in zero page. The vertical arm still uses 'sta w16+1' / 'lda w16+1' (3+3). Same rewrite applies to the low byte: 'sta w16' / 'lda w16' become tax/txa, because X's earlier value (the low byte of spy-refy) has already been consumed by the 'txa' two lines above and nothing reads w16 before @nc overwrites it. Flags: sta sets none, tax/tay do set N,Z, but in both places the very next instruction (tya, sbc) sets flags itself or reads only C, and transfers leave C untouched, so the sbc chain is unaffected. The final 'txa' leaves exactly the N,Z and value that 'lda w16' left, so the following 'asl' still puts the old bit 7 into C as the comment claims. Net 4 cycles and 4 bytes per drawsprite call.

assumption: X and Y are dead from this point to the next explicit ldx/ldy in drawsprite (they are: the next uses are 'ldx curbuf' and 'ldy #5' further down, both loads), and w16/w16+1 are dead here because the very next block rewrites both with lb1.
original:
sbc tmp3
        sta w16+1
        txa
        sec
        sbc wy
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        sbc wy+1
        sta sp_lb0+1
        lda w16
proposal:
sbc tmp3
        tay                         ; high byte in Y, as the horizontal arm above does
        txa
        sec
        sbc wy
        tax                         ; low byte in X: w16 was only a temp for the asl
        tya
        sbc wy+1
        sta sp_lb0+1
        txa
argument: This is the vertical arm of a pattern the horizontal arm (just above, at @cpos's predecessor) already does the cheap way: there the intermediate high byte is parked in Y with 'tay'/'tya' rather than in w16+1. The vertical arm stages both halves through zero page instead. sta w16+1 (3) -> tay (2), sta w16 (3) -> tax (2), lda w16+1 (3) -> tya (2), lda w16 (3) -> txa (2): 12 cycles of zero-page traffic become 8 of register moves, 4 cycles and 4 bytes. Flags: sta sets nothing and lda sets N,Z, which the following sbc overwrites; tay/tax/tya/txa set N,Z and leave C alone, so the borrow chain from 'sbc wy' into 'sbc wy+1' is unchanged, and the final txa leaves the same N,Z the 'lda w16' did before the asl (the asl overwrites them anyway and takes C from bit 7 of the same value). Y=5 is consumed by the preceding 'sbc (ptr),y' and is not read again before the later 'ldy #5'; the horizontal arm proves the same overwrite is safe with Y=4. w16 is dead: the next lines (lda sp_ext / deca / clc / adc sp_lb0 / sta w16 ... sta w16+1) rewrite both bytes with lb1 before any read. Path: @vert is entered for every sprite that survives horizontal clipping, i.e. essentially every drawn sprite, once per sprite per frame.

assumption: qx is written nowhere in logic.s between player_update's own 'mov16 qx, px' (logic.s:1236) and this point: the only calls on that path are getaltitude, gravity and vy_step, and getaltitude -> getinfo -> tilexy/maptile -> maprow/mapbyte only read qx (maprow/mapbyte use mapptr, engine.s:3483-3499). A grep of the whole source shows qx written only at logic.s:1075, 1236, 1299, 1331, 1487 and 1497-1504, none of which lie on that path.
argument: This is the 'push out of the ceiling' loop in player_update, entered whenever dpx is negative, i.e. every frame the player is moving upward. 'mov16 qx, px' is loop-invariant -- px does not change inside the loop and getaltitude modifies only qy (its own header says so, logic.s:367) -- and it is also already-done work: player_update opens with the identical 'mov16 qx, px' at logic.s:1236 and nothing between there and here writes qx. So the four zero-page loads/stores (3+3+3+3 = 12 cycles, 8 bytes) are pure recomputation. Deleting them leaves @upl starting at 'clc', which is the correct entry for the loop-back branches 'bne @upl' and 'bra @upl' (both local to this routine, no other reference to @upl exists). Flags: the deleted mov16 ends in 'sta qx+1' which sets no flags, and the instruction that now follows the preceding 'add16 py, dpx' is 'clc', so nothing reads a flag across the cut. Saving is 12 cycles per execution of the @up path, plus a further 12 for each extra iteration of the correction loop.

assumption: getaltitude does not write qx. Checked: getaltitude touches qy only (its own header says '[qy modified]'), and its callees getinfo, tilexy, maptile, maprow and mapbyte read qx but never write it -- the only `inc qx`/`dec qx` in logic.s are at lines 1497-1504, in a different routine.
argument: @upl is a loop: `jsr getaltitude / sta alt / bpl @vdone / inc py / bne @upl / inc py+1 / bra @upl`, pushing the player down a pixel at a time until the feet are out of the ground. Every pass rebuilds both halves of the probe point, but only qy changes -- qx is px on every pass, and px is not touched inside the loop. mov16 qx, px is lda px / sta qx / lda px+1 / sta qx+1 = 12 cycles; hoisting it above @upl leaves the first pass costing exactly what it costs now (the same four instructions, just before the label instead of after it) and removes 12 cycles from every additional pass. Byte count is unchanged -- the instructions move, none are added or removed. Correctness: the only flag-consuming instruction in the moved region is none at all; `clc` at the new @upl sets C unconditionally, so whatever flags add16 or the mov16 left are dead either way, and A is reloaded by `lda py` two instructions later. @upl has exactly two references, the `bne @upl` and `bra @upl` below it, both still landing on the qy rebuild. No anonymous label is added or removed. Frequency: player_update runs once a frame and the @up arm is taken whenever dpx is negative, but extra passes happen only when the feet are still inside a tile after the upward step, so the 12 cycles are per extra pass, not per frame -- a free, byte-neutral win on the frames where the loop actually spins.

assumption: w16+1 is dead from here to its next write. Verified by reading every path out of this point: both the c0-negative arm and @cpos read only w16 (never w16+1) before 'bra @vert', and the first thing @vert does with w16+1 is store to it ('lda spy+1 / sbc tmp3 / sta w16+1'). The only call in between, 'jsr sext', touches A and tmp3 only. A grep of engine.s confirms the next w16+1 reference after line 1154 is the store at line 1200.
original:
cmp #$80
        ror a                       ; sign into bit 7, old bit 0 out to C
        sta w16+1
        ror w16                     ; arithmetic shift right 1 -> c0 (16 bit)
        cmp #0                      ; A still holds w16+1: just restore N,Z
proposal:
cmp #$80
        ror a                       ; sign into bit 7, old bit 0 out to C
        ror w16                     ; arithmetic shift right 1 -> c0 (16 bit)
        cmp #0                      ; A still holds w16+1: just restore N,Z
argument: c0 is computed as a 16-bit arithmetic shift right of sx, but only its low byte (w16) is ever consumed; the high byte is used solely as a live value in A, to classify c0 as 0, -1 or out of range. 'sta w16+1' therefore writes a value nobody reads. Deleting it saves 3 cycles and 2 bytes on every drawsprite call that reaches the horizontal clip (i.e. every visible sprite with sp_w != 0 -- the routine's main path, run once per sprite per frame). Bytes unchanged. The changed path is the no-carry arm of the 16-bit lb0 add, taken whenever sp_lb0's low byte does not carry out of '+ wfine' -- the majority of drawsprite calls, once per sprite per frame.

assumption: X is free at @sp -- the tail call m_addsprite/addsprite starts with 'ldx NSPR', so it neither needs nor preserves X -- and q1 is dead after this point (ob_walker tail-jumps into addsprite, which reads only A, spx and spy; q1 is a scratch always written before it is read).
original:
@sp:    sta q1
        lda otype
        cmp #5
        bne :+
        lda #67
        bra :++
:       lda #76
:       clc
        adc q1
        jmp m_addsprite
proposal:
@sp:    ldx otype                   ; the frame stays in A: no round trip through q1
        cpx #5
        bne :+
        adc #66                     ; C = 1 from the equal cpx, so this is A + 67
        bra :++
:       clc
        adc #76
:       jmp m_addsprite
argument: The routine has the frame number in A at @sp, spills it to q1 only so that A can be used to test otype, then adds it back. Testing otype in X instead keeps the frame in A the whole way, deleting 'sta q1' and 'adc q1' and letting the base be an immediate. On the otype==5 arm the 'cpx #5' that selected it has already set C=1 (cpx sets C when X >= operand, so equality gives C=1), so 'adc #66' with that carry is exactly A+67 and no clc is needed; on the other arm C is unknown (cpx leaves C = otype>=5) so the clc is kept before 'adc #76'. addsprite is entered with A = sprite id, which is what both arms now leave. Cycles: otype!=5 path 21 -> 15 (save 6), otype==5 path 23 -> 15 (save 8). Bytes 20 -> 16. Anonymous labels: the original has two ':' lines here and so does the proposal, with 'bra :++' still reaching the second one (now on the jmp), so the count is unchanged. Path: @sp is the single exit of ob_walker's draw tail, reached once per walker object per frame, on every arm (@f0/@f2/@f4/@f8 and the #6 arm all converge here).

assumption: X is dead at @sp. The nearest prior use is jsr inrange, documented as clobbering A and X, and addsprite reloads X from NSPR on entry, so no caller of ob_walker can be relying on it.
original:
@sp:    sta q1
        lda otype
        cmp #5
        bne :+
        lda #67
        bra :++
:       lda #76
:       clc
        adc q1
        jmp m_addsprite
proposal:
@sp:    ldx otype                   ; the frame stays in A and the base is added onto
        cpx #5                      ; it, so q1 need not be staged and reloaded
        bne :+
        clc
        adc #67
        bra :++
:       clc
        adc #76
:       jmp m_addsprite
argument: Path: both arms of ob_walker's sprite-id tail, reached once per walker object per logic frame (every route into @draw ends here). The saving is the same 6 cycles on each arm, so the split between otype 5 and otype 6 does not matter. The frame number is in A at @sp and the only reason it is spilled to q1 is that the otype test is done with lda/cmp. Testing with ldx/cpx leaves A alone, so the base can be added straight onto it. otype == 5 arm: sta q1 3 + lda otype 3 + cmp #5 2 + bne not taken 2 + lda #67 2 + bra :++ 3 + clc 2 + adc q1 3 + jmp 3 = 23 becomes ldx otype 3 + cpx #5 2 + bne 2 + clc 2 + adc #67 2 + bra :++ 3 + jmp 3 = 17. otype != 5 arm: sta q1 3 + lda otype 3 + cmp #5 2 + bne taken 3 + lda #76 2 + clc 2 + adc q1 3 + jmp 3 = 21 becomes ldx otype 3 + cpx #5 2 + bne taken 3 + clc 2 + adc #76 2 + jmp 3 = 15. The clc is duplicated rather than hoisted because cpx sets carry; each arm still clears it immediately before its own adc, exactly as the original did, so the add is unaffected by whatever carry the @fr/@f0/@f8 arms left. X is dead here: the last reader was jsr inrange, which the comment on inrange says clobbers A and X, and addsprite (via m_addsprite) loads X from NSPR itself. Y is not touched. Anonymous labels: two ':' lines before, two after, in the same order -- bne :+ still reaches the first and bra :++ the second -- so the count through logic.s is unchanged. Saves 3 bytes.

assumption: w16+1 is dead after the @right test (the only later reader of w16 is the 'sbc w16' clamp, which still gets w16 = 0 from the retained stz). Requires adding the named local label @wadd; no anonymous label is added or removed.
original:
lda wcx
        sta rc_x
        lda wcx+1
        sta rc_x+1
        stz w16
        stz w16+1
@right: lda w16+1
        bne @none                   ; rel >= 256 -> off right
        lda w16
        cmp #ROWCHARS
        bcs @none                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        adc rc_w
proposal:
lda wcx
        sta rc_x
        lda wcx+1
        sta rc_x+1
        stz w16
        lda #0                      ; rel = 0, so the two @right tests are known to
        clc                         ; pass: skip them with A and C already as @wadd
        bra @wadd                   ; wants them
@right: bne @none                   ; rel >= 256 -> off right (A and Z are still the
        lda w16                     ; sbc wcx+1 that bpl @right just tested)
        cmp #ROWCHARS
        bcs @none                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
@wadd:  adc rc_w
argument:
Two things, both on drawrect_clip, which runs once per erase rect in erase_rects and once per entry in the dirty-tile loop -- tens of calls a frame.

(1) The common path. @right is reached only by 'bpl @right', whose test is the 'sbc wcx+1' three instructions earlier; 'sta w16+1' and 'bpl' both leave the flags alone, so on entry to @right the Z flag already says whether w16+1 is zero. 'lda w16+1' is a reload of the value that set the flags being tested. Deleting it saves 3 cycles and 2 bytes on every call that is not left-clipped, which is nearly all of them. (grep confirms 'bpl @right' is the only reference to @right, so this is the only entry once the fall-through below is removed.)

(2) The left-clip arm. It ends 'stz w16 / stz w16+1' and then falls into @right, where it re-derives what it just stored: 'lda w16+1' is 0 so the bne is not taken, 'lda w16' is 0, 'cmp #ROWCHARS' passes (0 < 80) and leaves C = 0, and the adc then adds 0 to rc_w. Eighteen cycles to arrive at 'adc rc_w' with A = 0 and C = 0. The replacement produces A = 0 and C = 0 directly (lda #0 / clc / bra @wadd) in 10, saving 8 cycles on that arm. stz w16 is kept because the 'lda #ROWCHARS / sbc w16' clamp below still reads it; stz w16+1 goes because nothing reads w16+1 again (drawrect rebuilds both halves of w16 from rc_x before calling ringaddr).

Net bytes: -2 for stz w16+1, -2 for lda w16+1, +5 for lda #0 / clc / bra = one byte larger. @wadd is a cheap local label, so the '@right:' and ':' anonymous label below are untouched and the ca65 anonymous-label count through this routine is unchanged.

assumption: The four instructions above the window, `and #$80 / beq :+ / lda #$FF / : sta dpx+1`, are vy_step's sign extension of a single byte, so at `bmi @up` A is $00 or $FF and equals dpx+1. @up is entered only by that bmi and @cup only by the `bne @cup` being removed; both are cheap locals with no other reference in the routine.
original:
stz dpx+1
        rts
@up:    cmp #$FF                    ; <= -256
        bne @cup
        lda dpx
        cmp #<-MAXDWY
        bcs @cdone
@cup:   lda #<-MAXDWY
        sta dpx
        lda #$FF
        sta dpx+1
proposal:
stz dpx+1
        rts
@up:    lda dpx                     ; dpx+1 is $FF on this arm, so neither the
        cmp #<-MAXDWY               ; <= -256 test nor the clamp's rewrite of the
        bcs @cdone                  ; high byte can do anything
@cup:   lda #<-MAXDWY
        sta dpx
argument: vy_step sets dpx to the high byte of vy+128 and sign-extends it, so the 16-bit dpx is always in -128..127 and dpx+1 is $00 or $FF. Two consequences on the @up arm. First, `cmp #$FF / bne @cup` tests for dpx <= -256, which cannot happen: A at @up is the value just stored into dpx+1, and bmi was taken, so A is $FF and the bne is never taken. Removing the pair saves 4 cycles on every execution of the up arm and drops the entry to `@up: lda dpx`. Second, once that branch is gone @cup has a single predecessor, the `bcs @cdone` above it falling through, where dpx+1 is already $FF -- so `lda #$FF / sta dpx+1` writes $FF over $FF and can go too, another 5 cycles on the clamped path. Flags: @cup's tail now ends at `sta dpx`, which sets no flags, and falls into `@cdone: rts`; nothing downstream reads A or the flags, since vy_step's callers use dpx from memory. The remaining `lda dpx / cmp #<-MAXDWY / bcs @cdone` is untouched and still an unsigned compare on $80..$FF against $F8, which is what it was. `stz dpx+1` at @cdn is left in place: it is provably dead too (the `bne @cdn` above the window cannot fire, A being $00 there), but it costs only 3 cycles on the down clamp and keeps this edit free of any dependence on a line the quote does not contain. Frequency: vy_step runs once a frame from player_update's @move, and the up arm is taken on every frame the player is rising, so 4 cycles a rising frame and 9 on the ones where the rise is clamped to MAXDWY.

original:
lsr tmp3
        ror
        sec
        sbc #2
        bcs :+
        dec tmp3
proposal:
lsr tmp3
        ror
        sbc #1                      ; C = 0 out of the ror pair, so this is A - 2
        bcs :+
        dec tmp3
argument: @dur builds A/tmp3 = n*64 by starting from hi=n, lo=0 and shifting the pair right twice, then subtracting 2. The carry out of the second 'ror' is deterministic: A enters the sequence as 0, so after 'lsr tmp3 / ror' A = c0<<7 and the ror's carry-out is A's old bit 0 = 0; after the second 'lsr tmp3 / ror' A = c1<<7 | c0<<6 and the carry-out is again the old A's bit 0, which is 0 because A was c0<<7. So C = 0 unconditionally at the 'sec'. With C = 0, 'sbc #1' computes A - 1 - (1-C) = A - 2, exactly what 'sec / sbc #2' computed, and it leaves the same C (set iff A >= 2, which is what the following 'bcs :+ / dec tmp3' borrow fixup reads) and the same N,Z. The 'sec' line carries no label and is not a branch target, and no anonymous label is added or removed. Saving 2 cycles and 1 byte per call to @dur. @dur is entered by two 'jsr @dur' in build_sections plus the 'jmp @dur' tail of @lines which @emit calls, so it runs 2-4 times per build_sections, i.e. 2-4 times a frame -- call it 4-8 cycles a frame. Small, but free and unconditional. (Two other things in this window were checked and rejected: @nfull's r == 0 test cannot be turned into a reversed 'lda mulrowlo,y / cmp ringS' to invert the carry, because ringS's low byte legitimately borrows past mulrowlo[barq] for rows whose 80-multiple wraps a page -- e.g. barq=6, mulrowlo=224, r=40 gives ringS_lo=8 -- so the reversed compare would report r == 0 wrongly; and @subrow/@addrow at engine.s:2448 and 2460 have no callers anywhere in engine.s or logic.s, which is ~40 dead bytes but zero cycles, and deleting their ':' lines is exactly the anonymous-label hazard for no cycle gain.)

assumption: Y is dead here. The ground arm 20 lines above (logic.s:1365/1370) already uses tay/tya for exactly this step and converges on the same @nofric tail, so nothing downstream can be relying on Y.
original:
sta t16+1
        txa
        clc
        adc vx
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
proposal:
tay
        txa
        clc
        adc vx
        sta t16
        tya
argument: Two arms of the same routine doing the same job at different cost. The ground arm builds t16 = 3*vx as 'lda vx/asl/tax/lda vx+1/rol/tay/txa/clc/adc vx/sta t16/tya/adc vx+1/sta t16+1'; the @air arm builds it identically except that it parks the high half in memory ('sta t16+1' then 'lda t16+1') instead of in Y. sta zp + lda zp is 6 cycles and 4 bytes; tay + tya is 4 cycles and 2 bytes. Flags: tya sets N and Z but leaves C alone, exactly like the 'lda t16+1' it replaces, so the carry from 'adc vx' still reaches 'adc vx+1' intact - this is the same reasoning that makes the ground arm correct. The final 'sta t16+1' at the end of the quoted run is unchanged, so t16+1 ends up with the same value. Saves 2 cycles and 2 bytes on the @air arm, executed once per player_update (once per frame) whenever the player is airborne or standing on a tile with no push, i.e. the majority of frames; the ground arm is already in this form.

assumption: gy still holds q2>>3 when @t0's tail runs: the prologue sets it at level_init's 'lda q2 / lsr / lsr / lsr / sta gy', and nothing between -- the otype dispatch chain, and @t0's own lda q3 / sta O_EL,y / lda q4 / sta O_EH,y / jsr m_rnd / jsr mod12 / sta O_AL,y / inc stars -- writes gy (the only writers of gy in the whole of logic.s are inside level_init, and mod12's scratch is q1).
original:
lda q2
        beq :+
        deca
:       lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta gy
        lda q2
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta gy1
        jmp @box
proposal:
lda gy                      ; the prologue already left q2>>3 in gy
        sta gy1
        lda q2
        beq :+
        deca
:       lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta gy
        jmp @box
argument: @t0 wants gy = (q2-1)>>3 and gy1 = q2>>3. But q2>>3 is exactly what the shared prologue already stored in gy a few instructions earlier, so the second 'lda q2 / lsr / lsr / lsr / sta gy1' recomputes a value that is sitting in a zero-page byte. Copying gy into gy1 first and only then overwriting gy with the decremented form gives the same two results. This is the same trick @t1 already uses two arms further down ('lda gy1 / sta gy'). Cycles: lda gy (3) + sta gy1 (3) = 6 replaces lda q2 (3) + three lsr (6) + sta gy1 (3) = 12, so 6 cycles on both the q2==0 and q2!=0 branches, and 3 bytes. Flags: nothing after the deleted sequence reads flags -- the next instruction is 'jmp @box' -- and the moved-up lda/sta pair sets N,Z before the 'lda q2 / beq' that needs them, so the beq still tests q2. Anonymous labels: one ':' line before and after, count unchanged. Path: @t0 is the star-object arm of level_init, run once per star object at level load.

assumption: spy does not alias oy or fc (spy is engine.s zero page at its own .res 2; oy = $AA, fc = $B0), so the intermediate copy carries no information the fused add does not.
original:
mov16 spy, oy
        add16 spy, fc
proposal:
clc                         ; spy = oy + fc in one pass, the way the ox + fd
        lda oy                      ; code twelve lines below already does it
        adc fc
        sta spy
        lda oy+1
        adc fc+1
        sta spy+1
argument: 'mov16 spy, oy' followed by 'add16 spy, fc' copies oy into spy (lda/sta/lda/sta = 12 cycles, 8 bytes) and then reads spy straight back to add fc to it (clc/lda/adc/sta/lda/adc/sta = 20 cycles, 13 bytes). Adding oy and fc directly into spy is the same seven instructions as the add16 alone: 20 cycles, 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles and 8 bytes. The carry chain is identical -- clc then adc low, adc high -- and the routine already does exactly this for the other coordinate twelve lines further on ('clc / lda ox / adc fd / sta spx / lda ox+1 / adc fd+1 / sta spx+1'), so the two arms of ob_rsnake's @knocked draw were doing the same job at different cost. The quoted pair is unique in the file (the other 'mov16 spy, oy' sites are followed by 'add16 spy, rise' or by 'lda #60'). No flags are consumed after the sequence (the next instruction is 'lda q1'), no anonymous label is involved, and this is a rank-0 path, so the 12 cycles are correctness-free but cold.

assumption: A is dead on return from square. The only call site is logic.s:2404 (the snake rise calculation), which reads t16/t16+1 only. X is the loop counter in both forms and is already destroyed.
original:
square: sta q1
        sta q1x
        stza t16
        stza t16+1
        ldx #8
@l:     asl t16
        rol t16+1
        asl q1
        bcc :+
        lda t16
        clc
        adc q1x
        sta t16
        bcc :+
        inc t16+1
:       dex
        bne @l
        rts
proposal:
square: sta q1
        sta q1x
        lda #0                      ; accumulator low byte lives in A
        stza t16+1                  ; stz never touches A on a 65C02
        ldx #8
@l:     asl
        rol t16+1
        asl q1
        bcc :+
        clc
        adc q1x
        bcc :+
        inc t16+1
:       dex
        bne @l
        sta t16
        rts
argument: The shift-and-add keeps its 16-bit accumulator entirely in memory, re-loading and re-storing the low byte through t16 every iteration. Holding the low byte in A instead costs nothing: A is otherwise unused across the whole loop. Per iteration 'asl t16' (5 cycles, 2 bytes) becomes 'asl' (2 cycles, 1 byte), saving 3 cycles x 8 iterations = 24. On each iteration whose q1 bit is set, 'lda t16 / clc / adc q1x / sta t16' (11 cycles) becomes 'clc / adc q1x' (5), saving 6 x (number of set bits k). Setup/teardown costs 2: 'stza t16 / stza t16+1' (6) becomes 'lda #0 / stza t16+1' (5, and stz never touches A on a 65C02 so A stays 0) plus a 'sta t16' after the loop (3). Total 22 + 6k; k = 4 gives 46. Carry chain is unchanged - 'rol t16+1' still takes the carry out of the accumulator shift, and the 'bcc :+' after 'adc q1x' still skips 'inc t16+1' on no carry. Flags on exit are the same (dex's Z; sta sets none). Anonymous-label count is unchanged: one ':' line, still the target of both bcc's. FREQUENCY CAVEAT: the window is ranked 0 and there is a single caller, logic.s:2404 inside the snake object's update, so this is worth 46 cycles per call on a level that has snakes and nothing at all otherwise. Correct and strictly cheaper, but do not count it against the frame budget.

original:
asl
        clc
        adc tmp3                    ; i*3
proposal:
asl
        adc tmp3                    ; i*3
argument: The clc is dead. Entering this line A = tmp3, which was written by 'stx tmp3' from the loop counter X, and the loop runs X = 0..5 (menu.s:394, 412-415), so tmp3 <= 5. 'asl' therefore shifts a 0 out of bit 7 and leaves C = 0, which is exactly what the following 'adc tmp3' needs; the 'adc #5' after it is already relying on the same argument (2*tmp3 + tmp3 <= 15, no carry). Removing the clc saves 2 cycles and 1 byte. Nothing else reads C between the asl and the adc, and no other branch enters between them. The path is the body of the six-line help text loop, so 12 cycles per help_screen call - the window is ranked 0 because help_screen runs once when the player opens the help page, so this is correctness-free tidying rather than a frame-budget saving.

assumption: bge16 is the exact complement of blt16 (macros.txt: identical lda/cmp/lda/sbc/bvc/eor sequence, differing only in the final bpl vs bmi), so inverting the test and dropping the 'bra' preserves semantics. ANONYMOUS LABEL CHANGE: this removes two ':' labels (the ones on 'inc fc' and 'inc fd'). I checked every anonymous reference in ob_bat (logic.s:2540-2700): they are all forward ':+' or ':++' whose targets lie entirely before or entirely after the removed labels -- 'bne :+' at 2572 targets the ':' on 'dec fc', and the 'bgt16 spx, px, :+' / 'bra :++' pair near 2643 targets the two ':' labels around 'inc q1'. There are no backward ':-' references anywhere in the routine, so no branch is retargeted.
original:
blt16 fc, fa, :+
        bra @ydir
:       inc fc
        bne @ydir
        inc fc+1
        bra @ydir
@rxpos: beq16 rx, @ydir
        beq16 fc, @ydir
        bmi16 fc, @ydir
        lda fc
        bne :+
        dec fc+1
:       dec fc
@ydir:  bpl16 ry, @rypos
        blt16 fd, fb, :+
        bra @boom
:       inc fd
        bne @boom
        inc fd+1
        bra @boom
proposal:
bge16 fc, fa, @ydir
        inc fc
        bne @ydir
        inc fc+1
        bra @ydir
@rxpos: beq16 rx, @ydir
        beq16 fc, @ydir
        bmi16 fc, @ydir
        lda fc
        bne :+
        dec fc+1
:       dec fc
@ydir:  bpl16 ry, @rypos
        bge16 fd, fb, @boom
        inc fd
        bne @boom
        inc fd+1
        bra @boom
argument: ob_bat's chase logic. Both the x arm and the y arm use the pattern 'blt16 a, b, :+ / bra @tail / : inc a', i.e. a signed compare whose false case pays a taken branch to reach the tail. Inverting the compare to bge16 and branching directly to the tail removes the 'bra' entirely. Per arm: when the compare is false (fc >= fa) the old code paid 'bmi' not taken (2) plus 'bra @ydir' (3) = 5 and the new pays 'bpl' taken (3), saving 2; when it is true the old paid 'bmi' taken (3) to reach 'inc fc' and the new pays 'bpl' not taken (2) and falls straight into it, saving 1. So it is never worse on either path. The bge16 expansion is the same length as blt16, so the 2 bytes saved per arm are exactly the deleted 'bra'. Branch range: from the new 'bpl @ydir' to @ydir is 8 bytes, and from the new 'bpl @boom' to @boom is about 30 bytes, both far inside the +/-128 window that the deleted 'bra' already spanned. Which arm runs is decided by 'bpl16 rx, @rxpos' / 'bpl16 ry, @rypos' just above, so each arm is taken on roughly the frames where the bat is on the far side of the player; per ob_bat call the total is 2 to 4 cycles. Note the window's cost rank is 0 -- bats do not appear in the profiled scene -- so this is correct but not measurable there. (I also considered making @rxpos mirror @rypos's cheaper 'lda fc+1 / bmi / ora fc / beq' form in place of 'beq16 fc' + 'bmi16 fc', which is 3 cycles cheaper when fc > 0 but 2 cycles dearer when fc == 0; without knowing which dominates I left it alone.)

assumption: Neither 'lda tmp4' nor the beq disturbs X, and neither arm writes X between the hoisted tax and its shr16x/shr24x call (the win arm does lda/sta on w16 only, the lose arm lda/sta on w16 and w16b only).
original:
@loop:  ; big cleo frame
        lda tmp4
        beq @lframe
        ; win: 4 + ((441 >> (n & 30)) & 3)
        lda tmp3
        and #30
        tax
        lda #<441
        sta w16
        lda #>441
        sta w16+1
        jsr shr16x
        lda w16
        and #3
        ora #4
        bra @drawc
@lframe:
        lda tmp3
        and #30
        tax
proposal:
@loop:  ; big cleo frame
        lda tmp3                    ; the shift count is the same on both arms
        and #30
        tax
        lda tmp4
        beq @lframe
        ; win: 4 + ((441 >> (n & 30)) & 3)
        lda #<441
        sta w16
        lda #>441
        sta w16+1
        jsr shr16x
        lda w16
        and #3
        ora #4
        bra @drawc
@lframe:
argument: Both arms of the win/lose selector start with the identical three instructions 'lda tmp3 / and #30 / tax' to build the shift count for shr16x / shr24x; only the constant that gets shifted differs. Hoisting them above the 'lda tmp4 / beq @lframe' test leaves one copy serving both arms. Correctness: X is set before the tmp4 test and read only by the jsr that each arm makes, and nothing in between touches X ('lda tmp4', the beq, and the immediate/zero-page stores of w16, w16+1, w16b all leave X alone). The tmp4 test itself is unaffected because 'and #30' and 'tax' have no bearing on the subsequent 'lda tmp4', which sets its own N,Z. Saving is 3+2+2 = 7 cycles and 5 bytes on whichever arm runs -- every iteration of @loop, i.e. once per frame for as long as the win/lose screen is displayed.

assumption: t16+1 is dead after these two sites - the only later writer/reader in ob_bat is the @dead arm, which sets both bytes itself before blt16 reads them - and X is not needed across the adds (it is reloaded by the 'tax' between them and dead after the second batoff fetch).
original:
lda batoff,x
        sx16 t16
        add16 spx, t16
        lda frame
        asl
        asl                         ; A = 5*frame, low byte only: the high byte of
        clc                         ; 5*frame is dead (the >>2 below shifts the low
        adc frame                   ; byte alone, and sx16 t16 rewrites both bytes)
        lsr
        lsr
        sta t16
        lda obj
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sec
        sbc obj
        clc
        adc t16
        and #15
        tax
        lda batoff,x
        sx16 t16
        add16 spy, t16
        lda q1
proposal:
lda batoff,x
        bpl @wx1                    ; spx += a signed byte, without building the word:
        dec spx+1                   ; pre-borrow the high byte when it is negative
@wx1:   clc
        adc spx
        sta spx
        bcc @wx2
        inc spx+1
@wx2:   lda frame
        asl
        asl                         ; A = 5*frame, low byte only: the high byte of
        clc                         ; 5*frame is dead (the >>2 below shifts the low
        adc frame                   ; byte alone, and only t16's low byte is used)
        lsr
        lsr
        sta t16
        lda obj
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sec
        sbc obj
        clc
        adc t16
        and #15
        tax
        lda batoff,x
        bpl @wy1
        dec spy+1
@wy1:   clc
        adc spy
        sta spy
        bcc @wy2
        inc spy+1
@wy2:   lda q1
argument:
Both wobble terms sign-extend a table byte into a word and then run a full 16-bit add. Adding a signed byte to a word does not need the word: pre-decrement the high byte when the byte is negative, add the low bytes, and carry.
Cost of one site now: sx16 = sta t16 3 + and #$80 2 + beq 3/2 + (lda #$FF 2) + sta t16+1 3, i.e. 11 positive / 12 negative; add16 = clc 2 + lda spx 3 + adc t16 3 + sta spx 3 + lda spx+1 3 + adc t16+1 3 + sta spx+1 3 = 20. Total 31 / 32, and 23 bytes.
Cost of the replacement: positive, no carry out = bpl taken 3 + clc 2 + adc 3 + sta 3 + bcc taken 3 = 14; positive with carry = 18; negative = bpl nt 2 + dec 5 + clc 2 + adc 3 + sta 3 + bcc nt 2 + inc 5 = 22. 13 bytes.
batoff (logic.s:2736) is 0,1,1,2,2,2,1,1,0,-1,-1,-2,-2,-2,-1,-1: ten non-negative entries and six negative, and for a negative entry the low-byte add carries out for all but |v| of the 256 low bytes. Weighted, a site costs about 17 against 31.4, so roughly 14 cycles saved per site and about 29 per bat per frame on the @draw path, which is the path every live bat takes every frame. 20 bytes saved.
Correctness: verified against the two awkward cases - b=$FD with spx=$0100 gives dec to $0000, $FD+$00=$FD with no carry, result $00FD = $0100-3; b=$FD with spx=$0105 gives $0005, $FD+$05=$02 with carry, inc to $0102. sta sets no flags and both following instructions are 'lda', so no flag is carried out. X and Y are untouched.
I used named cheap locals (@wx1/@wx2/@wy1/@wy2, none of which clash with the existing @boom/@dead/@done/@draw/@f0/@f2/@fr/@kill/@nostomp/@player/@rxpos/@rypos/@ydir in ob_bat) rather than anonymous labels, so the anonymous-label count in the file is unchanged - the two ':' lines this deletes are the ones inside the two sx16 expansions, each of which contained its own matching 'beq :+'.
Frequency caveat: the window is ranked at cost 0, i.e. no bat executed in the profiled level, so the measured gain on that level is zero; the figure above is per bat per frame wherever bats are present.

assumption: X is the mark_dirty buffer loop index, which the routine itself initialises with 'ldx #0' and advances with 'inx / cpx #2 / bne @b', so X is 0 or 1 on every pass.
original:
asl                         ; x*32
        clc
        adc tmp3
proposal:
asl                         ; x*32 -- X is 0 or 1, so the fifth asl cannot
        adc tmp3                    ; carry out and the clc is dead
argument: The carry entering 'adc tmp3' is provably already clear, twice over. First: X is the two-buffer loop counter, set by 'ldx #0' at the head of mark_dirty and only ever incremented to 1 ('inx / cpx #2 / bne @b'), so 'txa' loads 0 or 1 and the five asls shift 1 up to 32 -- bit 7 is never set before any of them, so none of the five produces a carry, and the last one leaves C=0. Second, independently: the path reaches here only through 'lda DIRTYCNT,x / cmp #16 / bcs @next' falling through, which means DIRTYCNT < 16 and C=0 from the cmp, and the following 'asl' on a value below 16 also clears C; 'sta tmp3' and 'txa' do not touch C. So the clc can go. The asl chain's own flags are not read (the next flag consumer is the adc's own result, and 'tay' after it sets N/Z from A, unchanged). Saves 2 cycles and 1 byte per pass of the two-buffer loop. Caveat on value: mark_dirty does not execute at all in the profiled run (linecost is 0 for every line of it), so this is a correctness-safe tidy rather than a frame-time win.

assumption: addsprite takes its sprite id in A only -- it opens with `ldx NSPR` and builds Y from sprmul5,x -- so nothing downstream needs X to hold 65/66.
original:
ldx #65
        bgt16 spx, px, :+
        bra :++
:       ldx #66
:       txa
        jmp m_addsprite
proposal:
bgt16 spx, px, :+
        lda #65
        bra :++
:       lda #66
:       jmp m_addsprite
argument: The two arms pick a sprite id into X and then funnel through a single `txa`; since the only consumer is A, load the id straight into A and delete the `txa`. addsprite (engine.s:976) starts `ldx NSPR` / `cpx #MAXSPR` / `ldy sprmul5,x`, so X is dead across the call, and the m_addsprite bridge is only `jsr addsprite / jmp pagelogic`. Cycles, not-taken arm (spx <= px, id 65): old ldx #65 2 + bra 3 + txa 2 = 7; new lda #65 2 + bra 3 = 5, saving 2. Taken arm (spx > px, id 66): old ldx #65 2 + ldx #66 2 + txa 2 = 6; new lda #66 2 = 2, saving 4. Bytes 7 -> 6. Flags: the bgt16 expansion (lda px / cmp spx / lda px+1 / sbc spx+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / bmi) is untouched and is the last flag consumer; the `lda #imm` after the branch sets N,Z but nothing reads them before the jmp. Anonymous labels are unchanged in number and position -- the macro's own ':' plus the two here -- so the macro's `bmi :+` still targets the id-66 arm and `bra :++` still targets the jmp. Path: the tail of ob_bat, once per active bat per frame. The window's cost rank is 0, so on the measured scene this is worth nothing; it only pays on levels with bats on screen, which is why the figure quoted is the not-taken arm's 2 cycles.

assumption: mod16 does not depend on the carry or on N/Z at entry -- which the first arm, twelve lines earlier, already proves: it reaches mod16 straight off an adc #0 / sta t16b+1.
original:
lda O_BL,y
        sta t16b
        lda O_BH,y
        sta t16b+1
        inc t16b
        bne :+
        inc t16b+1
:       jsr mod16
proposal:
clc
        lda O_BL,y
        adc #1
        sta t16b
        lda O_BH,y
        adc #0
        sta t16b+1
:                                   ; placeholder - keeps the anonymous-label count
        jsr mod16
argument: Two arms of @t4 do the same job -- form t16b = field + 1 for mod16 -- at different cost. The C arm (twelve lines above, unchanged) writes clc / lda O_AL,y / adc #1 / sta t16b / lda O_AH,y / adc #0 / sta t16b+1 = 2+4+2+3+4+2+3 = 20 cycles, 15 bytes. The D arm copies first and then increments in place: lda O_BL,y / sta t16b / lda O_BH,y / sta t16b+1 / inc t16b / bne :+ = 4+3+4+3+5+3 = 22 cycles and 16 bytes on the 255-in-256 path where O_BL is not $FF (when it is, the bne falls through and inc t16b+1 makes it 26). Rewriting it in the C arm's form makes it 20 cycles flat, saving 2 cycles and 1 byte, and makes the two arms textually identical apart from the field. Correctness: the sum is the same 16-bit value; O_BL/O_BH are read before either is written so there is no aliasing; mod16 begins with sec and so ignores the carry the adc #0 leaves, exactly as it already does on the C arm's path. LOUD FLAG on the anonymous label: the original's ':' labels the jsr mod16 line and is the target of this arm's own bne :+. Deleting it would retarget every :+/:++ that counts past this point, so the proposal keeps a bare ':' placeholder line -- the same device blt16i/bge16i/ble16i already use in macros.txt -- and the anonymous-label count is unchanged. Path and frequency: this is the @t4 (type-4 object) initialisation arm of level_init, executed once per type-4 object at level load, so the saving is 2 cycles per such object and the window's cost rank is 0. It is a correctness-neutral tidy-up of a real cost asymmetry, not a frame-time win.
